proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(M\in MC(A,B)\), and write \(\mathbb P_M\) for its induced law \(PM\).  Under \(\operatorname{do}(Z=0)\), the structural equation for \(X\) is unchanged, so \(X=Xn\).  Hence \(\text{ass:regime-a-match}\) and normalization of \(A\) give
\[
\mathbb P_M(Xn=0)
=\sum_{y\in D}\mathbb P_M(X=0,Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=0))
=A(0,0)+A(0,1)=p.
\]
Similarly, under \(\operatorname{do}(X=0)\), \(Z=Zn\), and \(\text{ass:regime-b-match}\) gives
\[
\mathbb P_M(Zn=0)=B(0,0)+B(0,1)=r.
\]
By \(\text{ass:independent-roots}\), \(U0\) and \(V0\) are independent.  Therefore their measurable images \(Xn=fX(U0)\) and \(Zn=fZ(V0)\) are independent, because for every \((i,j)\in D^2\),
\[
\mathbb P_M(Xn=i,Zn=j)
=\mathbb P_M(fX(U0)=i)\mathbb P_M(fZ(V0)=j).
\]
Using the two preceding marginal identities yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P_M(Xn=0,Zn=0)&=pr=w00,\\
\mathbb P_M(Xn=0,Zn=1)&=p(1-r)=w01,\\
\mathbb P_M(Xn=1,Zn=0)&=(1-p)r=w10,\\
\mathbb P_M(Xn=1,Zn=1)&=(1-p)(1-r)=w11.
\end{aligned}
\]

On the event \(\{Xn=0\}\), surgical substitution under \(\operatorname{do}(Z=0)\) gives
\[
Y=fY(Xn,0,U0,V0,W0)=fY(0,0,U0,V0,W0)=Y00.
\]
Partitioning this event by \(Zn\) and using \(\text{def:natural-response-masses}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
a=A(0,1)
&=\mathbb P_M(Xn=0,Y00=1)\\
&=s(0,0)+s(0,1).
\end{aligned}
\]
The symmetric substitution on \(\{Zn=0\}\) under \(\operatorname{do}(X=0)\) gives
\[
b=B(0,1)=\mathbb P_M(Zn=0,Y00=1)=s(0,0)+s(1,0).
\]
Writing \(c=s(0,0)\) and \(d=s(1,1)\), these equations force
\[
(s(0,0),s(0,1),s(1,0),s(1,1))=(c,a-c,b-c,d).
\]
Since the four events \(\{Xn=i,Zn=j\}\) partition the sample space,
\[
q=\mathbb P_M(Y00=1)=\sum_{i,j\in D}s(i,j)=a+b-c+d.
\]

For each stratum, success mass lies between zero and total stratum mass.  Thus
\[
0\le c\le w00,\qquad 0\le a-c\le w01,\qquad
0\le b-c\le w10,\qquad 0\le d\le w11.
\]
The first three pairs of inequalities are jointly equivalent to
\[
\max\{0,a-w01,b-w10\}=cL\le c\le
\min\{w00,a,b\}=cU.
\]
Conversely, any \(c,d\) satisfying these displayed bounds makes the four displayed masses nonnegative and no larger than their corresponding \(w_{ij}\).  This proves the asserted exact parameterization at the mass-accounting level.

First suppose \(MC(A,B)\neq\varnothing\), and take \(M\in MC(A,B)\).  By \(\text{lem:four-stratum-reduction}\), its value \(c=s(0,0)\) satisfies \(cL\le c\le cU\); hence \(cL\le cU\).

Conversely, if \(cL\le cU\), choose \(c=cL\) and \(d=0\).  Since \(w11>0\), this pair belongs to \(F(A,B)\).  The source-preserving lift then supplies a model \(M\in MC(A,B)\), so the class is nonempty.  Thus
\[
MC(A,B)\neq\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad cL\le cU.
\]

It remains to simplify this condition.  Strict positivity and normalization imply
\[
0<a<p=w00+w01,\qquad 0<b<r=w00+w10.
\]
For \(cL=\max\{0,a-w01,b-w10\}\) to be at most \(cU=\min\{w00,a,b\}\), every lower candidate must not exceed every upper candidate.  All such comparisons are automatic from the preceding inequalities and nonnegativity, except
\[
a-w01\le b\qquad\text{and}\qquad b-w10\le a.
\]
Indeed, for example, \(a-w01\le w00\) follows from \(a\le w00+w01=p\), while \(b-w10\le w00\) follows from \(b\le w00+w10=r\); comparisons with \(a\) or \(b\) themselves use \(w01,w10\ge0\).  The two nonautomatic comparisons are equivalent to
\[
a-b\le w01=p(1-r),\qquad a-b\ge-w10=-(1-p)r.
\]
This proves both stated equivalences, including equality cases.

Assume \(MC(A,B)\neq\varnothing\).  For any \(M\in MC(A,B)\), the four-stratum reduction gives a pair
\[
(c,d)\in[cL,cU]\times[0,w11]
\]
and the identity \(q=a+b-c+d\).  Consequently every compatible value obeys
\[
a+b-cU\le q\le a+b-cL+w11.
\]
The two endpoints simplify by elementary min--max algebra:
\[
\begin{aligned}
a+b-cU
&=a+b-\min\{w00,a,b\}\\
&=\max\{a+b-w00,b,a\}=qL,
\end{aligned}
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
a+b-cL+w11
&=a+b+w11-\max\{0,a-w01,b-w10\}\\
&=\min\{a+b+w11,b+w01+w11,a+w10+w11\}\\
&=\min\{a+b+(1-p)(1-r),b+1-r,a+1-p\}=qU,
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(w01+w11=1-r\) and \(w10+w11=1-p\).

To prove attainment of every point, let \(q_\star\in[qL,qU]\), put
\[
\delta:=q_\star-qL,\qquad C:=cU-cL,
\]
and define
\[
v:=\min\{\delta,C\},\qquad c:=cU-v,qquad d:=\delta-v.
\]
Compatibility gives \(C\ge0\), and the endpoint calculation gives
\[
0\le\delta\le qU-qL=C+w11.
\]
Thus \(0\le v\le C\), whence \(cL\le c\le cU\).  If \(\delta\le C\), then \(d=0\); if \(\delta>C\), then \(d=\delta-C\le w11\).  Therefore \((c,d)\in F(A,B)\).  Moreover,
\[
a+b-c+d=(a+b-cU)+v+(\delta-v)=qL+\delta=q_\star.
\]
The source-preserving lift constructs one finite member of \(MC(A,B)\) attaining this value.  Hence the image defining \(QI(A,B)\) is exactly the complete closed interval \([qL,qU]\), not merely a convex outer bound.

Suppose all cells of \(A\) and \(B\) are rational and the pair is compatible.  Then \(p,r,a,b\), all \(w_{ij}\), and the max--min values \(cL,cU\) are rational.  By the endpoint calculation in \(\text{thm:sharp-risk-interval}\), the lower endpoint is obtained from
\[
(c,d)=(cU,0),
\]
and the upper endpoint from
\[
(c,d)=(cL,w11).
\]
For either pair, every ratio
\[
\frac{c}{w00},\quad \frac{a-c}{w01},\quad
\frac{b-c}{w10},\quad \frac{d}{w11},\quad
\frac{A(1,1)}{1-p},\quad \frac{B(1,1)}{1-r}
\]
is rational; all denominators are strictly positive.  In the source-preserving lift, the ordered thresholds \(\lambda_k\) are therefore rational, so every private-root mass \(\lambda_k-\lambda_{k-1}\) is rational.  The binary-root masses \(p,1-p,r,1-r\) are rational as well, while \(fX,fZ,fY\) are deterministic.  The lift hence gives rational-weight endpoint models with \(|\operatorname{supp}(W0)|\le8\).

There are at most
\[
|\operatorname{supp}(U0)|\,|\operatorname{supp}(V0)|\,
|\operatorname{supp}(W0)|\le2\cdot2\cdot8=32
\]
exogenous assignments.  Enumerating these assignments, multiplying their rational product weights, applying the deterministic functions under each intervention, and summing verifies every experimental cell and the endpoint exactly.  Thus each endpoint model is the claimed finite rational certificate.

For a fixed pair of \(2\times2\) tables, forming \(p,r,a,b\) uses a fixed number of cell accesses and additions.  The two compatibility sides use two multiplications and a fixed number of additions, subtractions, and comparisons.  Conditional on compatibility, evaluating the three candidates for each of \(qL\) and \(qU\), followed by one maximum and one minimum over three numbers, again uses a fixed number of arithmetic operations and comparisons.  By \(\text{thm:compatibility-frontier}\) and \(\text{thm:sharp-risk-interval}\), these outputs are respectively the correct compatibility decision and the sharp endpoints.

For rational inputs, the corrected construction of \(Cert\) forms two fixed endpoint pairs, at most seven response probabilities, and sorts at most nine rational thresholds for each endpoint.  These are bounded-size operations independent of the numerical values.  By \(\text{prop:rational-endpoint-certificates}\), the resulting product-root tables and deterministic response maps are exact endpoint certificates, each involving at most \(32\) exogenous assignments.  Therefore the operation count is constant for this fixed graph and query.  This is an arithmetic-operation statement; it does not assert unit bit complexity for rationals of unbounded encoding length.

The endpoint identities proved in \(\text{thm:sharp-risk-interval}\) give
\[
qL=a+b-cU,
\qquad
qU=a+b-cL+w11.
\]
Subtracting yields
\[
qU-qL=cU-cL+w11.
\]
Compatibility gives \(cU-cL\ge0\).  Strict positivity of both tables gives \(0<p,r<1\), and hence
\[
w11=(1-p)(1-r)>0.
\]
Therefore \(qU-qL\ge w11>0\).  Since the sharp identified set is \([qL,qU]\), it contains more than one value of \(q\); thus the two supplied experiments do not point-identify the joint-intervention risk anywhere in the stated strictly positive compatible model.

For the displayed tables,
\[
p=\frac18+\frac38=\frac12,
\qquad
r=\frac38+\frac18=\frac12,
\qquad
a=\frac38,
\qquad
b=\frac18.
\]
Every displayed cell is positive, and \(w00=w01=w10=w11=1/4\).  Hence
\[
cL=\max\left\{0,\frac38-\frac14,\frac18-\frac14\right\}=\frac18,
\qquad
cU=\min\left\{\frac14,\frac38,\frac18\right\}=\frac18.
\]
The endpoint formulas give
\[
qL=\frac38+\frac18-\frac18=\frac38,
\qquad
qU=qL+\frac14=\frac58.
\]

For an explicit pair of certificates, let \(U0,V0\) be independent fair binary roots and set \(X=U0\), \(Z=V0\).  In both models use
\[
t_{00}=\frac12,qquad t_{01}=1,qquad t_{10}=0,qquad
\gamma_A=\gamma_B=\frac14,
\]
and use \(t_{11}=0\) for the lower model and \(t_{11}=1\) for the upper model.  The distinct thresholds are contained in \(\{0,1/4,1/2,1\}\), so one may take a private root \(W0\), independent of \((U0,V0)\), with three masses \(1/4,1/4,1/2\), and use the deterministic threshold function from the source-preserving lift.  This is one deterministic outcome function within each endpoint model and it is used in all regimes.

For either endpoint model, direct summation gives the four \(A\)-cells
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P_M(X=0,Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=0))&=\tfrac14(\tfrac12)+\tfrac14(1)=\tfrac38,\\
\mathbb P_M(X=0,Y=0\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=0))&=\tfrac12-\tfrac38=\tfrac18,\\
\mathbb P_M(X=1,Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=0))&=\tfrac12(\tfrac14)=\tfrac18,\\
\mathbb P_M(X=1,Y=0\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=0))&=\tfrac12-\tfrac18=\tfrac38,
\end{aligned}
\]
and the four \(B\)-cells
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P_M(Z=0,Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=0))&=\tfrac14(\tfrac12)+\tfrac14(0)=\tfrac18,\\
\mathbb P_M(Z=0,Y=0\mid\operatorname{do}(X=0))&=\tfrac12-\tfrac18=\tfrac38,\\
\mathbb P_M(Z=1,Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=0))&=\tfrac12(\tfrac14)=\tfrac18,\\
\mathbb P_M(Z=1,Y=0\mid\operatorname{do}(X=0))&=\tfrac12-\tfrac18=\tfrac38.
\end{aligned}
\]
Finally, the joint-intervention success mass is
\[
\frac14\left(\frac12+1+0+t_{11}\right),
\]
which equals \(3/8\) when \(t_{11}=0\) and \(5/8\) when \(t_{11}=1\).  Thus the independent-root endpoint models agree with all eight cells exactly and certify the asserted identified interval.

Write \(n_A:=nA\), \(n_B:=nB\), \(\widehat A:=Ah\), and \(\widehat B:=Bh\), and define
\[
\varepsilon_A:=\sqrt{\frac{\log(16/alpha)}{2n_A}},
\qquad
\varepsilon_B:=\sqrt{\frac{\log(16/alpha)}{2n_B}}.
\]
Thus \(eps=\max\{\varepsilon_A,\varepsilon_B\}\).  For each fixed cell of \(A\), its empirical frequency is the mean of \(n_A\) independent Bernoulli indicators by \(\text{ass:multinomial-a}\).  The cited Bernoulli Hoeffding inequality gives
\[
\Pr\bigl(|\widehat A(x,y)-A(x,y)|>\varepsilon_A\bigr)
\le2e^{-2n_A\varepsilon_A^2}=\frac{alpha}{8}.
\]
The same calculation under \(\text{ass:multinomial-b}\) holds for each cell of \(B\) with \(\varepsilon_B\).  A union bound over the eight cells therefore gives an event \(\mathcal E\) with
\[
\Pr(\mathcal E)\ge1-alpha
\]
on which every cell error in both tables is at most \(eps\).  This union bound does not require independence between the two experimental samples.

On \(\mathcal E\), letting hats denote summaries computed from the empirical tables,
\[
|\widehat a-a|\le eps,
\quad |\widehat b-b|\le eps,
\quad |\widehat p-p|\le2eps,
\quad |\widehat r-r|\le2eps.
\]
All empirical and population marginals lie in \([0,1]\), so
\[
|\widehat p\widehat r-pr|
\le \widehat p\,|\widehat r-r|+r|\widehat p-p|
\le4eps.
\]
Applying the same calculation to the complements gives
\[
|(1-\widehat p)(1-\widehat r)-(1-p)(1-r)|\le4eps.
\]
Consequently the three lower-endpoint branches have respective errors bounded by \(eps,eps,6eps\), and the three upper-endpoint branches have errors bounded by \(3eps,3eps,6eps\).  For any finite vectors \(u,v\),
\[
|\max_i u_i-\max_i v_i|\le\max_i|u_i-v_i|,
\qquad
|\min_i u_i-\min_i v_i|\le\max_i|u_i-v_i|.
\]
It follows that, on \(\mathcal E\),
\[
|qLh-qL|\le6eps,
\qquad
|qUh-qU|\le6eps.
\]

If \(MC(A,B)\neq\varnothing\), \(\text{thm:sharp-risk-interval}\) gives \(QI(A,B)=[qL,qU]\subseteq[0,1]\).  The preceding inequalities then imply
\[
\max\{0,qLh-6eps\}\le qL\le qU\le\min\{1,qUh+6eps\},
\]
so \(CIout\) contains the whole identified set and cannot be empty on \(\mathcal E\).  If \(MC(A,B)=\varnothing\), then \(QI(A,B)=\varnothing\) by definition and containment is automatic, including when the displayed empirical interval is interpreted as empty.  The max--min Lipschitz argument did not select a unique branch, so endpoint ties and population compatibility-boundary equalities require no additional condition.

theorem.statement: For every strictly positive pair \((A,B)\) for which \(F(A,B)\neq\varnothing\), and every \((c,d)\in F(A,B)\), the handle \(Hthr\) constructs a finite model \(M\in MC(A,B)\) with binary roots \(U0,V0\), a private root \(W0\) with at most eight support points, mutually independent roots, and one deterministic outcome function \(fY\) shared by all regimes, such that \(q=a+b-c+d\).  The construction reproduces all four cells of \(A\) and all four cells of \(B\).
theorem.proof_tex:
Fix strictly positive normalized tables \(A,B\) and \((c,d)\in F(A,B)\).  Strict positivity gives
\[
0<p<1,\quad 0<r<1,\quad 0<a<p,\quad 0<b<r,
\]
so all four numbers \(w00,w01,w10,w11\) are positive.  Define independent binary roots by
\[
\mathbb P(U0=0)=p,\qquad \mathbb P(V0=0)=r,
\]
and set \(fX(u)=u\), \(fZ(v)=v\).  Define
\[
t_{00}:=\frac{c}{w00},\quad
t_{01}:=\frac{a-c}{w01},\quad
t_{10}:=\frac{b-c}{w10},\quad
t_{11}:=\frac{d}{w11},
\]
and
\[
\gamma_A:=\frac{A(1,1)}{1-p},\qquad
\gamma_B:=\frac{B(1,1)}{1-r}.
\]
Membership in \(F(A,B)\), together with the equivalences proved in \(\text{lem:four-stratum-reduction}\), gives \(0\le t_{ij}\le1\).  Moreover,
\[
0<A(1,1)<A(1,0)+A(1,1)=1-p
\]
and the analogous inequality for \(B\) give \(0<\gamma_A,\gamma_B<1\).

For \((x,z,u,v)\in D^4\), prescribe the response probability
\[
h(x,z,u,v):=
\begin{cases}
t_{uv},& (x,z)=(0,0),\\
\gamma_A,& (x,z)=(1,0),\\
\gamma_B,& (x,z)=(0,1),\\
1/2,& (x,z)=(1,1).
\end{cases}
\]
The finite set
\[
\mathcal H:=\{t_{00},t_{01},t_{10},t_{11},\gamma_A,\gamma_B,1/2\}
\]
has at most seven elements.  List the distinct elements of \(\mathcal H\cup\{0,1\}\) in increasing order as
\[
0=\lambda_0<\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_m=1.
\]
There are at most nine listed numbers, so \(m\le8\).  Let \(W0\), independent of \((U0,V0)\), take values in \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\) with
\[
\mathbb P(W0=k)=\lambda_k-\lambda_{k-1},\qquad 1\le k\le m.
\]
These masses are positive and telescope to one.  For \(h\in\mathcal H\), define
\[
g(h,k):=\mathbf 1\{\lambda_k\le h\}.
\]
If \(h=\lambda_j\), including \(j=0\) or \(j=m\), then
\[
\mathbb P\{g(h,W0)=1\}
=\sum_{k=1}^{j}(\lambda_k-\lambda_{k-1})
=\lambda_j=h.
\]
Finally define the single deterministic structural function
\[
fY(x,z,u,v,k):=g(h(x,z,u,v),k).
\]
Thus the same \(fY\) and the same private root are used under every intervention, and the product construction makes \(U0,V0,W0\) mutually independent.

It remains to verify the complete experimental menu.  Under \(\operatorname{do}(Z=0)\), independence and the threshold identity give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P_M(X=0,Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=0))
&=pr\,t_{00}+p(1-r)t_{01}=c+(a-c)=a=A(0,1),\\
\mathbb P_M(X=1,Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=0))
&=(1-p)\gamma_A=A(1,1).
\end{aligned}
\]
The row probabilities of \(X\) are \(p\) and \(1-p\), so
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P_M(X=0,Y=0\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=0))&=p-a=A(0,0),\\
\mathbb P_M(X=1,Y=0\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=0))&=1-p-A(1,1)=A(1,0).
\end{aligned}
\]
Under \(\operatorname{do}(X=0)\), the analogous calculation is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P_M(Z=0,Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=0))
&=pr\,t_{00}+(1-p)r t_{10}=c+(b-c)=b=B(0,1),\\
\mathbb P_M(Z=1,Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=0))
&=(1-r)\gamma_B=B(1,1),\\
\mathbb P_M(Z=0,Y=0\mid\operatorname{do}(X=0))&=r-b=B(0,0),\\
\mathbb P_M(Z=1,Y=0\mid\operatorname{do}(X=0))&=1-r-B(1,1)=B(1,0).
\end{aligned}
\]
Hence all eight cells match and the constructed model lies in \(MC(A,B)\).  Under the joint intervention,
\[
\begin{aligned}
q
&=\sum_{i,j\in D}\mathbb P(U0=i,V0=j)t_{ij}\\
&=w00t_{00}+w01t_{01}+w10t_{10}+w11t_{11}\\
&=c+(a-c)+(b-c)+d=a+b-c+d.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the source-preserving lift, including the asserted support bound.
theorem.justification: The common threshold construction proves that every feasible mass pair lifts without coupling the two source roots.
theorem.gap: The lift is derived directly here because generic finite canonicalization does not itself provide this eight-point source-preserving certificate.
theorem.consumer: The theorem supplies the common-SCM attainment step for compatibility, sharpness, and exact endpoint certificates.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(T_1,\ldots,T_n\) be independent and identically distributed random variables taking values in \(\{0,1\}\), with \(\mathbb E[T_i]=\theta\), and let \(\overline T_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nT_i\).  For every \(t>0\),
\[
\Pr\bigl(|\overline T_n-\theta|\ge t\bigr)\le 2\exp(-2nt^2).
\]

source.locator: Theorem 2, inequality (2.6), specialized to variables in the unit interval and applied to both tails

attestation.note: Transcribed from Hoeffding (1963), Theorem 2, inequality (2.6); the displayed node is its Bernoulli two-tail specialization.

added_lemmas.justification: This classical finite-sample inequality controls each multinomial cell frequency.
added_lemmas.gap: This is cited classical substrate, not a contribution of the note.
added_lemmas.consumer: It is used only by the outer-confidence-interval proposition.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: On input \((A,B)\), compute \((p,r,a,b)\), return incompatible exactly when either \(a-b<-(1-p)r\) or \(a-b>p(1-r)\), and otherwise return \((qL,qU)\) from their three-branch formulas.  If all input cells are rational and the pair is compatible, also use \((c,d)=(cU,0)\) and \((c,d)=(cL,w11)\).  For each pair compute \(t_{00}=c/w00\), \(t_{01}=(a-c)/w01\), \(t_{10}=(b-c)/w10\), \(t_{11}=d/w11\), \(\gamma_A=A(1,1)/(1-p)\), and \(\gamma_B=B(1,1)/(1-r)\).  Use response probabilities \(t_{uv}\) when \((x,z)=(0,0)\), \(\gamma_A\) when \((x,z)=(1,0)\), \(\gamma_B\) when \((x,z)=(0,1)\), and \(1/2\) when \((x,z)=(1,1)\).  Sort the distinct elements of these probabilities together with \(\{0,1\}\) as \(0=\lambda_0<\cdots<\lambda_m=1\), give \(W0=k\) mass \(\lambda_k-\lambda_{k-1}\), take independent binary \(U0,V0\) with zero-probabilities \(p,r\), set \(fX(u)=u\), \(fZ(v)=v\), and set \(fY(x,z,u,v,k)=\mathbf 1\{\lambda_k\le h(x,z,u,v)\}\) for the just-specified response probability \(h\).  Emit the resulting two models \(M\in MC(A,B)\) as lower- and upper-endpoint certificates.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The frozen construction returned only a decision and endpoints, while the constant-time-certificate proposition also requires the procedure to emit rational endpoint witnesses.  The corrected construction makes that fixed-size output algorithm explicit.

proposed.construction: On input \((A,B)\), compute \((p,r,a,b)\), return incompatible exactly when either \(a-b<-(1-p)r\) or \(a-b>p(1-r)\), and otherwise return \((qL,qU)\) from their three-branch formulas.  If all input cells are rational and the pair is compatible, also use \((c,d)=(cU,0)\) and \((c,d)=(cL,w11)\).  For each pair compute \(t_{00}=c/w00\), \(t_{01}=(a-c)/w01\), \(t_{10}=(b-c)/w10\), \(t_{11}=d/w11\), \(\gamma_A=A(1,1)/(1-p)\), and \(\gamma_B=B(1,1)/(1-r)\).  Use response probabilities \(t_{uv}\) when \((x,z)=(0,0)\), \(\gamma_A\) when \((x,z)=(1,0)\), \(\gamma_B\) when \((x,z)=(0,1)\), and \(1/2\) when \((x,z)=(1,1)\).  Sort the distinct elements of these probabilities together with \(\{0,1\}\) as \(0=\lambda_0<\cdots<\lambda_m=1\), give \(W0=k\) mass \(\lambda_k-\lambda_{k-1}\), take independent binary \(U0,V0\) with zero-probabilities \(p,r\), set \(fX(u)=u\), \(fZ(v)=v\), and set \(fY(x,z,u,v,k)=\mathbf 1\{\lambda_k\le h(x,z,u,v)\}\) for the just-specified response probability \(h\).  Emit the resulting two models \(M\in MC(A,B)\) as lower- and upper-endpoint certificates.

proposed.statement: Under \(\text{ass:multinomial-a}\) and \(\text{ass:multinomial-b}\), with probability at least \(1-alpha\), \(CIout\) contains the complete population set \(QI(A,B)\), including at endpoint ties and compatibility boundaries.
proposed.justification: A simultaneous cellwise concentration layer gives a transparent conservative sampling guarantee without smooth-branch selection.
